**How to falsify it:** Absence of elevated glutamate levels in patients with dicarboxylic aminoaciduria, or conversely, presence of dicarboxylic aminoaciduria in patients with gain-of-function GLS mutations. _(variant: GnomAD frequency > 0.01 for common variants in GLS associated with gain-of-function phenotypes.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the link between amino acid metabolism and neurological/developmental disorders could inform therapeutic strategies targeting metabolic pathways to ameliorate disease symptoms. Specifically, interventions to reduce glutamate excitotoxicity in the context of GLS gain-of-function mutations might be explored.
